name: BambooHR
whyPeoplePay: BambooHR sells the feeling that HR admin is handled. One employee record that payroll, benefits, time off and performance all read from, an onboarding checklist that runs itself, and reporting a founder can actually use, wrapped in an interface that does not need training. That coherence is genuinely hard to build and harder to keep. What you rent alongside it is a bill that grows with headcount whether or not anyone logs in: it is priced per employee per month, the plan ladder puts performance management on the second rung and benchmarking on the third, and payroll, benefits administration, time and attendance and global employment are four separately quoted add-ons beside it. Every plan button on the pricing page says Get Quote.

plans.name: Core
plans.note: $10 USD per employee per month for companies over 25 employees. Employee records, custom reports, workflows, documents, an AI assistant over your own HR data. Companies of 25 or fewer pay a flat rate starting at $250 USD/mo instead.

plans.name: Pro
plans.note: $17 USD per employee per month. Everything in Core plus performance management, 360 review cycles and 1:1s, and an AI assistant that can also answer from your policies and handbooks.

plans.name: Elite
plans.note: $25 USD per employee per month. Everything in Pro plus benchmark data and analysis, AI-powered data insights, and the premium service items: administrator training sessions, data integrity hours, extra implementation days.

pricing.note: Read live off the pricing page on 2026-08-14, where the three plan cards carry the figures and the FAQ repeats them in prose. Two things the ladder does not show. Companies with 25 employees or fewer are billed a flat rate starting at $250 USD/mo rather than per employee, which is why the swap on the OrangeHRM page assumes 25 people: $10 x 25 is exactly that floor. And the four add-ons, Payroll, Benefits Administration, Time & Attendance and Global Employment, carry no price at all on the page, so a real quote for a company that wants payroll is above these figures by an amount the page will not tell you. The page also notes automatic volume discounts, a 15% discount for registered nonprofits, and a 15% bundle discount for combining Payroll and Benefits Administration with any plan, US employees only. Every plan card's button reads Get Quote, so these are list prices at the start of a sales conversation.

ranked.rationale: The only honest answer here, and it is a narrower one than BambooHR. OrangeHRM Starter is GPL-3.0 and self-hostable in full, with the employee record, leave, time and attendance, recruitment, performance, a corporate directory and reporting in the box, plus LDAP and OpenID Connect sign-in that most vendors would sell you. What it does not have, by its own vendor's comparison, is onboarding, training, surveys, career development, request desk, rostering and discipline, all of which sit in the quote-only Advanced edition, and there is no payroll in either. Two containers, a MariaDB you back up, and an install that ends with a browser wizard you have to claim yourself, because the command line installer refuses unattended mode. Attachments are capped at 1 MB by a constant in the source, which matters if documents were the reason you were leaving.

evaluatedNotTested.name: Horilla
evaluatedNotTested.note: The liveliest of the newer options and the one with the interface designed this decade: recruitment, onboarding, attendance, leave, payroll and performance in one Django application, with an official image on Docker Hub. GitHub reports the licence as LGPL-2.1, while the README badge points at LGPL-3.0, which is the sort of ambiguity worth resolving before you commit a company's personnel records to it. Development is genuinely active, with the last push to its default branch on 2026-08-14 and 1.6.1 released on 2026-07-29, but it is a younger project than OrangeHRM by seventeen years and its release history is shorter than the retention period of the data you would put in it. No container from us yet.

evaluatedNotTested.name: Frappe HR
evaluatedNotTested.note: The most capable free HR product in this list and the one we are least willing to hand a first-time self-hoster. GPL-3.0, 8.5k stars, released constantly (v16.16.0 on 2026-08-07), and it does the thing OrangeHRM Starter will not: payroll, with salary structures, tax slabs and payslips, plus onboarding, appraisals and expense claims. The cost is the platform underneath it. Frappe HR is an app on the Frappe framework, not a standalone service, and upstream's own Docker compose brings up eleven services: two databases, two Redis instances, a websocket process, a scheduler, two queue workers, a configurator, a site creator and an nginx front end. Its manual path starts with bench and `bench get-app erpnext`. That is a stack to operate, not an install to finish, and it belongs on its own page rather than as a footnote here.
